title: In-Register Fused FP8 NVFP4 GEMM For SM120 Blackwell
original_idea: Port PLAQuant single-kernel mixed-precision fused GEMM from SM80 (INT4+INT8) to SM120 (RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell). SM120 uses mma.sync.aligned (not tcgen05/TMEM) but natively supports MXFP8 block-scaled (m16n8k32, E4M3, UE8M0 scale per 32 K) and NVFP4 block-scaled (m16n8k64, E2M1, UE4M3 scale per 16 K). Both atoms share identical FP32[4] accumulator registers with SM80_16x8_Row CLayout — enabling direct in-register accumulation across phases (same pattern as existing SM80 fused kernel). Key differences from the original SM100 plan: no TMEM, no WGMMA, 99KB SMEM (not 228KB), no cluster multicast, GDDR7 1.8TB/s (not HBM3e 8TB/s). The algorithmic layer (ResQ PCA + variance split + Stiefel rotation) is unchanged. CUTLASS already provides SM120 CollectiveBuilder support (examples 79/87). Hardware: 8x RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB GDDR7 each, CUDA 13.0). Target: single-kernel FP8+FP4 fused GEMM beating both FP16 cuBLAS and 2-launch FP baseline on LLM shapes (Llama 1B/3B/8B).
synthesis_notes: The primary direction (direct SM80→SM120 port) is the critical path, but the alternatives form a natural pipeline: once the kernel works, Alt-3 (algorithm co-design) provides the FP-aware quantization to feed it optimal data, Alt-1 (tile tuning) optimizes the kernel for GDDR7 bandwidth characteristics, and Alt-4 (end-to-end integration) wires everything into a real inference path. Alt-2 (CuTe DSL) could accelerate tile exploration if the Python DSL toolchain is confirmed available. The strongest synthesis is: port the kernel first (primary), immediately validate with the existing format spec and fake quantizers from Alt-3, tune tiles per Alt-1's bandwidth analysis, then integrate end-to-end per Alt-4. All alternatives contribute to the final deliverable rather than being mutually exclusive.

directions.name: Direct SM80→SM120 Kernel Port
directions.rationale: The most natural path: mechanically translate the existing mixed_gemm_l20.cu dual-phase shared-accumulator architecture from INT MMA to FP block-scaled MMA, reusing the SMEM-union and two-phase loop pattern.
directions.raw_phase3_response:
## APPROACH_SUMMARY

Port the existing SM80 INT4+INT8 dual-phase fused GEMM kernel (`kernels/mixed_gemm_l20/mixed_gemm_l20.cu`) to SM120 by replacing:
- **INT4 mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k64 → MXFP4 (NVFP4) mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k64** (E2M1 element, E4M3 block scale per 16 K)
- **INT8 mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32 → MXFP8 mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32** (E4M3 element, E8M0 block scale per 32 K)
- Keep the SM80-style architecture: SMEM union (not TMEM), two-phase sequential loop (low→high), shared FP32[4] accumulator registers, single epilogue

Core mechanism: SM120 mma.sync atoms share identical CLayout (FP32[4] Row accumulator) with SM80_16x8_Row — enabling the exact same dual-phase in-register accumulation pattern.

Keep the SM80-style architecture: SMEM union, two-phase sequential loop, shared FP32[4] accumulator registers, single epilogue.

directions.name: Bandwidth-Optimized Tile Strategy
directions.rationale: Focus on the GDDR7 1.8TB/s constraint (vs 8TB/s HBM3e); design tile shapes, software-pipelining depth, and SMEM staging specifically to maximize bandwidth utilization within the 99KB SMEM budget.
directions.raw_phase3_response:
## APPROACH_SUMMARY

Tile FP8+FP4 dual-phase fused GEMM for SM120 Blackwell with 99KB SMEM budget. Core mechanism: union SharedStorage reuse like SM80 kernel, but tune tile/stages specifically for GDDR7 1.8TB/s bandwidth. Key findings: (1) Small M (≤128) is compute-bound on SM120, shallow pipeline sufficient; (2) Large M (≥512) becomes bandwidth-bound; (3) 128×128 tile + 5 stages = 48KB SMEM (48% utilization), leaves headroom for cross-phase prefetch.
directions.approach_summary: Tile FP8+FP4 dual-phase fused GEMM for SM120 Blackwell with 99KB SMEM budget. Tune tile/stages specifically for GDDR7 1.8TB/s bandwidth. 128×128 tile + 5 stages main/4 stages high = 48KB SMEM (48% utilization), leaves headroom for larger K tiles or cross-phase prefetch optimization.

directions.name: Algorithm-Kernel Co-Design
directions.rationale: Exploit the FP format change to co-optimize the ResQ quantization pipeline: adjust high_fraction, block size alignment, and rotation training specifically for FP8/FP4 noise characteristics and SM120's per-block-scale granularity.
directions.raw_phase3_response:
## APPROACH_SUMMARY

Extend promix/quantize/basis.py to compute MXFP8/NVFP4 quantization noise metrics per variance segment during eigendecomposition; use these to guide adaptive high_fraction selection; tune optimize_rotation.py training to incorporate FP quantization noise (replace INT quantizers with MXFP8/NVFP4 variants in ActQuantWrapper during SGDG training).

## OBJECTIVE_EVIDENCE

- promix/quantize/quant_utils.py:29-90 — FP format infrastructure with stubs
- promix/quantize/optimize_rotation.py:233-254 — Rotation training hook for FP quantizers
- promix/quantize/basis.py:94-503 — Eigenvalue file for variance profile
- docs/specs/spec-mxfp8-nvfp4.md — Block-scale alignment constraints
- promix/configs/llama-3.2-1b-resq.yaml:11 — high_fraction global knob

## KNOWN_RISKS

- FP fake quantizer stubs not implemented
- Block-size alignment constraints need validation
- Rotation training cost amplification
- No SM120 hardware for kernel validation
- FP vs INT noise mismatch may not generalize

## CONFIDENCE

medium

directions.name: End-to-End Inference Integration
directions.rationale: Focus on the full inference pipeline: weight packing, online activation quantization, kernel invocation, and epilogue dequant — building on the existing promix/inference/ infrastructure to deliver end-to-end speedup, not just kernel-level.
directions.raw_phase3_response:
## APPROACH_SUMMARY

Build end-to-end inference pipeline on existing promix/inference/ infrastructure (~536 LOC). Implement SM120 kernel with PyBind11 interfaces, extend real_forward.py for FP8/FP4 dispatch, add MXFP8/NVFP4 block-scale computation to quant_ops.py, extend benchmark.py for latency measurement.

## OBJECTIVE_EVIDENCE

- promix/inference/weight_packer.py (77 LOC) — splits W main/high, quantizes, packs
- promix/inference/real_forward.py (164 LOC) — activation quantize → split → pack → kernel call → epilogue dequant
- promix/inference/quant_ops.py (94 LOC) — per-token/per-channel quantization ops
- promix/inference/benchmark.py (200 LOC) — full latency harness
- docs/specs/spec-mxfp8-nvfp4.md — scale composition formula
- promix/eval/ptq.py — FP format detection branch exists

## KNOWN_RISKS

- CUTLASS SM120 support uncertain in third_party/cutlass/
- MXFP8/NVFP4 numeric types not confirmed in CUTLASS headers
- Block scale tensor management (2D arrays) has no precedent in SM80 codebase
- Epilogue scale composition complexity
- 99KB SMEM constraint

## CONFIDENCE

medium
